findings.evidence: Mathlib names complement-headed conclusions `compl_iUnion`, `compl_iInter`, and `compl_support_eq_sUnion`; the naming guide requires theorem names to follow the written operation order.
findings.fix: Rename them `compl_posRoots` and `negRoots_eq_compl`, following the conclusion outward.
findings.issue: `posRoots_compl` and `negRoots_compl` (line 60) obscure which expression is complemented; the former concludes `(posRoots P b)ᶜ = …`, while the latter concludes `negRoots P b = (posRoots P b)ᶜ`.

findings.evidence: Lines 117–118 show the mismatch; the adjacent line-108 counterpart actually has the advertised membership proposition.
findings.fix: Either state `P.reflectionPerm i i ∈ posRoots P b` or rename the lemma to describe `IsPos`.
findings.issue: `reflectionPerm_self_mem_posRoots_iff_mem_negRoots` advertises membership in `posRoots`, but its left side is the predicate `b.IsPos (P.reflectionPerm i i)`.

summary: Three public theorem names do not accurately follow the syntactic form of their conclusions.
